Deploying AI
AI makes people who can direct it more powerful. The messier parts that AI can't do become bottlenecks.
Use AI tools in your current job. Work at companies solving real problems with AI.
Personal effectiveness
Productivity, social skills, and rapid learning are useful in every job and compound the value of your other skills.
Use AI tutors to rapidly teach you new skills. Work with people who have these skills. Develop good habits.
Leadership skills
Management, strategy, and research taste are messy tasks AI struggles with, but AI gives leaders more influence than before.
Seek mentorship. Work at small, growing organisations, and seek small-scale management positions. Otherwise, start side projects. Study and apply best practice.
Communications and taste
Content creation gets automated, but discernment and trusting relationships with your audience become more valuable.
Build an authentic audience. Focus on personality-driven content. Work with people who have taste.
Getting things done in government
Citizens want real people making decisions, so knowing how to get things done in government remains crucial (even if many civil service positions disappear).
Follow standard routes into policy: staffer positions, internships, fellowships, government positions, and working with successful operators.
Complex physical skills
Robotics lags behind knowledge work, especially for specialist work in unpredictable environments.
Seek apprenticeships in growing fields (e.g. datacentre construction), or just get an entry-level job.
In contrast, the future for these skills seems a lot more uncertain:
Coding, applied math, and STEM
Routine white collar skills such as recall and application of established knowledge, routine writing, admin, and translation
Visual creation such as animation.
More routine physical skills such as driving
It’s hard to say what effect this will have on the job market overall, or how quickly it will unfold, but it seems likely that relatively entry-level white collar jobs such as in law, finance, tech, government, healthcare, and professional services will struggle, in favour of an expanded class of leaders overseeing AI agents, and with increasing wages. Small teams and individuals will have more leverage than before. Retail, manual, and physical presence jobs (e.g. police, teacher, surgeon, construction worker) in the bottom half of incomes will be relatively unaffected (incomes roughly keeping pace with GDP) at least until robotics catches up. On average, wages initially rise, but could eventually come under pressure.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在数据存储或传输时，应选择使用明文（plaintext）还是哈希值（hashes）

不同观点：
• 支持使用哈希值的观点：
  - 哈希值可以有效保护数据隐私，因为原始数据无法直接从哈希值中推导出来。
  - 哈希值在验证数据完整性方面非常有用，可以用来检测数据是否被篡改。
  - 举例：密码存储中常用哈希值来避免直接保存明文密码，防止泄露。

• 支持使用明文的观点：
  - 明文数据在某些场景下更容易理解和使用，特别是在需要直接读取和处理数据的场合。
  - 明文传输或存储在某些简单应用中可能更加高效，不需要额外的计算资源来生成和验证哈希。
  - 举例：在非敏感信息的传输中，使用明文可能更加便捷且没有安全顾虑。

• 对两种方法的折中观点：
  - 可以在不同场景下结合使用明文和哈希值，例如在需要保护隐私和验证完整性时使用哈希，而在需要直接访问数据时使用明文。
  - 建议在安全要求高的系统中使用哈希值，而在开发、测试或低风险环境下使用明文以提高效率。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于数据的安全性与可访问性、计算成本之间的平衡。
- 另一个值得注意的点是，使用哈希值虽然提升了安全性，但仍需防范哈希碰撞和彩虹表攻击等风险。
- 实际应用中，选择还可能受到法规、合规要求以及具体业务需求的影响。

Sixteen billion passwords to
Apple
,
Facebook
,
Google
, and other
social media accounts,
as well as government services, were leaked in what researchers are calling the largest data breach ever, according to reports.
The leak exposed 16 billion login credentials and passwords, prompting both Google to tell billions of users to change their passwords and the FBI to warn Americans against opening suspicious links in SMS messages, according to a report published Thursday in
Forbes.
Researchers at
Cybernews
, who have been investigating the leak, found “30 exposed datasets containing from tens of millions to over 3.5 billion records each.”
All but one of these datasets have not been previously reported as being exposed, so the data impacted is all considered new.
“This is not just a leak – it’s a blueprint for mass exploitation,” the researchers said. And they are right. These credentials are ground zero for phishing attacks and account takeover. “These aren’t just old breaches being recycled,” they warned, “this is fresh, weaponizable intelligence at scale.”
Sixteen billion passwords to Apple, Facebook, Google and other accounts were leaked in what researchers have called the largest data breach ever.
(
Alamy/PA
)

Most of that intelligence was in the format of a URL, followed by logins and passwords. That information then allowed access to “pretty much any online service imaginable, from Apple, Facebook, and Google, to GitHub, Telegram, and various government services.”
While worrisome, the researchers found that the datasets were exposed very briefly – with enough time for them to be discovered, but not long enough for researchers to figure out who was controlling the data.
Researchers have determined the leak is the work of multiple infostealers, but it’s impossible to tell how many people or accounts were exposed, according to Cybernews.
The experts urge people to invest in password management solutions, not share their passwords and to stay alert in the event their passwords are compromised.

data.title: Elliptic Curves as Art
data.author: nill0
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Nadir Hajouji和Steve Trettel的一个项目，旨在可视化椭圆曲线（elliptic curves）。目前，该项目的网页正在建设中，邀请访问者耐心等待。文章还提到了一些相关的学术论文和精美的椭圆曲线图示。该项目旨在通过艺术形式展示数学概念，将抽象的椭圆曲线形象化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对椭圆曲线和零知识证明（zk proofs）可视化的不同观点和讨论，包括其美学价值、实用性、技术细节以及可能的应用场景。

不同观点：
• [欣赏与赞美]  
  - **cosmodev**: 作为长期从事椭圆曲线和零知识证明工作的人，认为这些可视化非常棒，视其为“极客艺术”。
  - **tempodox**: 称赞可视化让数学对象看起来像物理实体，甚至可以3D打印。
  - **ykonstant**: 原本预期会失望，但发现可视化不仅美观而且实用，尤其几何特性保留得很好，并推荐了相关论文。
  - **aanet**: 简单表达了对可视化作品的喜爱，认为非常漂亮。
  - **bedit**: 认为将抽象数学转化为视觉艺术很有趣，期待进一步的发展。
  - **gloosx**: 联想到自然界中的椭圆曲线，比如花朵，认为这些图像很吸引人。
  - **knottedoak**: 认为这些可视化对理解模性定理和费马大定理有很大帮助。

• [艺术与商业联想]  
  - **matcha-video**: 提到区块链上的程序化艺术，并引用了Tyler Hobbs的作品作为例子。
  - **felineflock**: 开玩笑地说想把图像印在T恤上，但担心被误认为外星甜甜圈店的品牌。
  - **broken_broken_**: 表示想买印有这些图像的T恤。

• [技术疑问与讨论]  
  - **charlieyu1**: 提出关于有限域上的椭圆曲线可视化的疑问，质疑其离散性如何呈现。
  - **larodi**: 提到与其他数学可视化工具（如Structure Synth和Context Free Art）的潜在联系，探讨了语法形式主义和椭圆曲线之间的数学联系。
  - **loxias**: 询问这些图像是否是用Blender渲染的，表现出对具体实现方法的好奇。
  - **Datagenerator**: 请求分享源代码，以便能够重现这些美丽的图像。

• [个人联想与感受]  
  - **HappMacDonald**: 联想到拓扑学中的球面反演过程，认为这些图像看起来像是该过程的中途状态。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：尽管评论整体积极，但**charlieyu1**对有限域上的椭圆曲线可视化的技术细节提出了疑问，这是评论中唯一对技术实现表示困惑的地方。
- 艺术与实用性：评论中不少人既赞赏了这些可视化的美学价值（如cosmodev、aanet），也有人强调了其实用性（如ykonstant、knottedoak）。
- 技术实现：多位评论者对可视化的具体实现方式（如3D打印、Blender渲染）表现出兴趣，并进行了相关讨论（tempodox、loxias、larodi）。

data.title: Getting Started Strudel
data.author: rcarmo
data.article_summary: Strudel是一个通过代码创作音乐的工具，是Tidal Cycles模式语言的JavaScript版本。无需JavaScript或Tidal Cycles基础即可使用。Strudel可用于实时编码音乐、算法作曲、教学以及集成到现有音乐设备中。它提供了一个交互式教程和REPL环境来帮助用户入门。用户可以通过代码控制样本、节奏和声音效果，创造丰富的音乐作品。文章还提供了代码示例和视频展示，帮助用户了解Strudel的潜力。学习Strudel的最佳起点是参与其工作坊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Strudel音乐工具的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• **积极评价与推荐**：
   - **milchek**：对Strudel的循环概念和音符数字表示方式印象深刻，认为这些功能使得旋律创作和即兴演奏变得有趣。同时提到Euclidean patterns的随机化支持，并推荐了Switch Angel的视频演示。
   - **jan_Inkepa**：赞赏编辑器在播放歌曲时高亮显示文件活跃部分的功能。
   - **dzink**：认为Strudel是一个低门槛且有趣的工具，既能创作音乐又能保存音乐创意，还能帮助人们轻松入门编程。

• **功能赞赏但文档批评**：
   - **henrebotha**：认为Strudel的流畅API和"display-oriented REPL"非常酷，但指出文档不足，API参考资料不全，功能发现性差，解释不权威。
   - **pwatsonwailes**：目前在使用Strudel的Superdough和transpiler部分，认为功能强大但文档不足。

• **其他体验与趣闻**：
   - **jarmitage**：分享了自己和Strudel合作发布的remix链接。
   - **whywhywhywhy**：认为Strudel的可视化反馈部分是一个很好的演示。
   - **joeatwork**：即使对用Strudel创作音乐不感兴趣，也推荐访问其网站以欣赏展示的多样音乐作品。

44287248.article_content:
Welcome
Welcome to the Strudel documentation pages!
Youâve come to the right place if you want to learn how to make music with code.
What is Strudel?
With Strudel, you can expressively write dynamic music pieces.
It is an official port of the
Tidal Cycles
pattern language to JavaScript.
You donât need to know JavaScript or Tidal Cycles to make music with Strudel.
This interactive tutorial will guide you through the basics of Strudel.
The best place to actually make music with Strudel is the
Strudel REPL
What can you do with Strudel?
live code music: make music with code in real time
algorithmic composition: compose music using tidalâs unique approach to pattern manipulation
teaching: focussing on a low barrier of entry, Strudel is a good fit for teaching music and code at the same time.
integrate into your existing music setup: either via MIDI or OSC, you can use Strudel as a really flexible sequencer
Examples
Here are some examples of how strudel can sound:
// "coastline" @by eddyflux
// @version 1.0
samples('github:eddyflux/crate')
setcps(.75)
let chords = chord("<Bbm9 Fm9>/4").dict('ireal')
stack(
stack( // DRUMS
s("bd").struct("<[x*<1 2> [~@3 x]] x>"),
s("~ [rim, sd:<2 3>]").room("<0 .2>"),
n("[0 <1 3>]*<2!3 4>").s("hh"),
s("rd:<1!3 2>*2").mask("<0 0 1 1>/16").gain(.5)
).bank('crate')
.mask("<[0 1] 1 1 1>/16".early(.5))
, // CHORDS
chords.offset(-1).voicing().s("gm_epiano1:1")
.phaser(4).room(.5)
, // MELODY
n("<0!3 1*2>").set(chords).mode("root:g2")
.voicing().s("gm_acoustic_bass"),
chords.n("[0 <4 3 <2 5>>*2](<3 5>,8)")
.anchor("D5").voicing()
.segment(4).clip(rand.range(.4,.8))
.room(.75).shape(.3).delay(.25)
.fm(sine.range(3,8).slow(8))
.lpf(sine.range(500,1000).slow(8)).lpq(5)
.rarely(ply("2")).chunk(4, fast(2))
.gain(perlin.range(.6, .9))
.mask("<0 1 1 0>/16")
)
.late("[0 .01]*4").late("[0 .01]*2").size(4)
These examples cannot fully encompass the variety of things you can do, so
check out the showcase
for some videos of how people use Strudel.
Getting Started
The best way to start learning Strudel is the workshop.

data.title: Ask HN: What do you think about app native vs. portable look-and-feel?
data.author: ttd
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同类型的用户界面（UI）在跨平台和原生应用开发中的优劣比较

不同观点：
• **pellenys** 认为原生UI的使用带来了更好的一致性和可用性。他指出，原生UI基于多年经验形成的标准，比如Windows应用中的tab顺序和取消按钮映射到escape键等惯例。虽然跨平台UI也能用且美观，但缺乏原生UI的那种统一性，现在的Electron应用（如Slack、Spotify、VSCode）看起来和用起来都很不一样，这让用户在使用不熟悉的应用时感到不便。不过，他也承认跨平台UI大大节省了开发工作量，而多数人可能并不像他这么在意这些细节。

• **not_your_vase** 强调效率和性能，认为平台特定的原生工具包在性能上几乎总是胜过跨平台UI。他反感看到大量的内存和CPU资源被浪费在简单的界面显示上，比如一个跑马灯效果也要消耗大量资源。

• **saluki** 认为跨平台UI（如React Native）在视觉和感觉上已经表现得很专业，尽管他仍然认为原生UI更好，但也能接受跨平台UI的表现。

• **brudgers** 持实用主义观点，认为只要应用有用，用户不会在意是否是原生UI。如果应用没用，即使使用原生UI也无济于事。他指出，开发者可能对这个问题有强烈意见，但这些意见只在特定情况下（如工作面试）重要。应用的质量问题往往出在其他更难解决的地方，而纠结于是否使用原生UI只会增加开发复杂性，不如专注于让应用“能用”就好。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：原生UI和跨平台UI在可用性、一致性、性能和开发效率上的取舍。pellenys和not_your_vase更关注原生UI的传统优势，而saluki和brudgers则更能接受跨平台UI的实用性和现代发展趋势。
- **性能问题**：not_your_vase特别提到了性能问题，认为跨平台UI往往在性能上不如原生UI，造成资源浪费。
- **开发效率**：brudgers和pellenys都提到跨平台UI在开发效率上的优势，认为这是其被广泛采用的主要原因之一。

data.title: Posit floating point numbers: thin triangles and other tricks (2019)
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过比较两种32位数字格式——IEEE binary32（即单精度浮点数）和posits（es=2），展示了它们在计算薄三角形面积时的表现差异。作者使用Heron公式计算三角形面积，并展示了精确值、posits计算结果和IEEE计算结果。结果显示，posits在精度上优于IEEE格式，尤其在处理细微差异时更为准确。文章还讨论了两种格式的历史背景和设计选择，指出IEEE格式在处理大数时精度不足，而posits则能在更大范围内保持较高精度。文章通过几个数值示例和幽默叙述，强调了posits在某些计算中的优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Posits与IEEE浮点数(FP)的比较及其在不同应用场景中的优劣

不同观点：
• dnautics（Posits的创建者之一）：
  - 认为Posits不适用于科学计算，因为误差传播问题难以解决。
  - Posits更适合机器学习(ML)中的低位表示，误差传播在此不重要。
  - 提到Facebook对Posits的修改（对数尾数）以及硬件实现的困难。
  - 强调Posits在特定应用（如AI）中的潜力。

• burnt-resistor：
  - 分享了一个类似IEEE格式的速查表，提供了对不同格式的测试结果。

• mserdarsanli：
  - 开发了一个交互工具展示Posits，认为Posits在某些情况下比IEEE浮点数有更好的精度表现，但也有权衡。

• adrian_b：
  - 认为Posits在某些示例中表现出的高精度具有误导性，因为其误差分布不均匀。
  - 指出Posits在靠近零的区间精度高，但在远离零的区间误差大。
  - 认为Posits在科学计算中不实用，因为难以预测和控制误差，且需要硬件支持才能实现最佳性能。

• antiquark：
  - 提到Posits与Unum类型III相关，提供了背景信息。

• phkahler：
  - 对Posits的兴趣不在精度，而在其没有符号零和NaN，认为操作结果不应是非数字。

• im3w1l：
  - 提出纯指数格式的可能性，认为这种格式可以避免一些特殊情况，如零和NaN的处理。

• andrepd：
  - 对讨论表示高度兴趣，认为帖子提供了深刻的见解。

补充讨论：
- Posits的误差传播和分布问题是一个争议焦点，特别是在科学计算和复杂计算中。
- 不同应用场景（如AI与科学计算）对数值表示格式有不同需求，Posits在特定应用中可能有优势。
- 硬件实现的困难和现有GPU管线的兼容性是Posits推广的一个实际障碍。
- 对IEEE浮点数的替代方案有多种提议，每种方案在不同应用中有其优缺点。

44319144.article_content:
February
6th,
2019
WARNING:
Some numerical analysis and mathematics will be mentioned in passing. Also the number systems will not be treated like black-boxes. Risk of physical injury, however, is negligible.
I like magic tricks. Watching the performer do the show and attempting to catch the “slight-of-hand” that makes the impossible seem possible. It’s fun and makes me believe in magic for a few moments. So I’m going to give a shot at doing some floating point magic tricks.
Throughout my performance I’ll use two 32-bit formats:  IEEE
binary32
(aka singles or
float
in a number of languages) and
posits
(with es=2).
NARRATOR:
For general purpose computations 32-bit is about as small as we can push, otherwise bit size choice doesn’t matter.  Gustafson uses
es=3
to cover the range of
binary32
but suggests that
es=2
is a better and it look like that’s the value they’re running with for the specification.  The choice doesn’t matter in the slightest for this discussion.
Originally this was going to be one big post but I’ve decided to break in in parts. Source code will be provided in a later version (for reasons). There are so many intertwined issues that it’s almost impossible to provide some nice linear presentation.
Goldberg’s long thin triangle
performance LIVE on stage
NARRATOR:
Kahan presented this problem in or prior to 1986 and the Goldberg paper (from 1991) was inspired from attended a conference by Kahan.
We are going totally compute the area $A$ of a thin triangle using the classic form of
Heron’s equation
. Life’s way too short to think about computation!
\[\begin{align*}
s & = \frac{a+b+c}{2} \\
A & = \sqrt{s\left(s-a\right)\left(s-b\right)\left(s-c\right)}
\end{align*}\]
With a wave of my hand I declare the lengths to be:
\[\begin{align*}
a & = 7 \\
b & = c= \frac{1}{2}\left(a+3~\text{ulp}\left(a\right)\right)
\end{align*}\]
and let’s pull out of my magic computationalizing box the exact, the
super-mojo-exponent
and
tapering-precision-just-exactly-where-you-need-it
posits and poor old
binary32
results (wrong digits in red):
\[\begin{align*}
\text{exact} & = 7.831550 \times 10^{-3} \\
\text{posit} & = 7.831550 \times 10^{-3} \\
\text{IEEE}  & = \color{red}{9.043097} \times 10^{-3}
\end{align*}\]
Booyah!
In your face ya old retired, don’t publish papers anymore, stuck in the 80s people! Posits are, like, exact and you got ZERO digits correct!
NARRATOR:
Attempting a detailed comparison between two formats which are both base-2 in base-10 is misleading.
Ahhh…okay.  Let’s look again:
\[\begin{align*}
\text{exact} & = 1000000001001111111001110 \times 2^{-31} \\
\text{posit} & = 100000000100111111100111\color{red}{1} \times 2^{-31} \\
\text{IEEE}  & = 100\color{red}{1010000101001011111110} \times 2^{-31}
\end{align*}\]
CAT-A-STROPIC!
only
3
out of 24 binary digits correct vs. 23!
NARRATOR:
Yes. I see what you did there. Very clever, but then again Gustafson titled his mathematica example
“Thin triangle area with posits: an unfair fight”
I’m going to do this trick again, but first I want to tell a story. Way back in 1985..raise your hand if you were even born yet. Yeah? A couple of people. Ok, well, back in the day integer adders were super cheap and integer multiplier super expensive SO the IEEE committee was all like
“Okay..let’s make the exponent part bigger (since that needs adders) and the fractional bits part smaller(that the multipliers)!”
.  I suppose that was fine then, but man-oh-man have things changed. Like we just saw…singles only have 24 bit of precision (AT MOST!) and totally fail at a simple computation.  But at the same time can represent really stupid big numbers! Get this: the largest finite number a single can represent is almost $2^{128}$. I think mathematicians call numbers like this googleperplexing…probably because even searching the web won’t help you understand them. See what I mean. Way too big.  That’s why I’m using posits with es=2. With that we still represent numbers up to $ {2^{120}} $ AND have more precision. Maybe a better choice would be to use es=3..that would slightly hurt our precision, but we’d be able to drop-in-replace IEEE doubles with 32-bit posits (how dope is that?)…but I’m going to stick with my choice for now.
NARRATOR:
Knuth once said:
“The idea that people knew a thing or two in the ’70s is strange to a lot of young programmers.”
Let’s do the same thing again, but this time with a reasonably big, but not googleperplexing, number: $a=3670016$.
\[\begin{align*}
\text{exact} & = 100000000100111111100111 \times 2^{8}              & \approx 2.1527203 \times 10^{9} \\
\text{posit} & = \color{red}{0}  \\
\text{IEEE}  & = 100\color{red}{101000010100101111111} \times 2^{8} & \approx 2.4857475 \times 10^{9}
\end{align*}\]
